═══ SESSION: 17 CLOSED · 12 CHANGES MERGED · eb6e PLAN NOW CERTIFIED AFTER FINDING A CUTOVER SHOWSTOPPER ═══

## EPIC STATE — derive it yourself, but this is what I left
38 descendants, 34 CLOSED. Remaining: eb6e (open, PLAN CERTIFIED, ready to claim), 8625 (open, BLOCKED by
eb6e), f124 + 2ca9 (in_progress, closes running as I write this).
OFF-EPIC satellites: 34cd (closing), 9ec0 (in_progress, an agent is implementing it).
main tip when I stopped: e9d4d390c3.

## MERGED THIS SESSION (12)
1286 7fe2 · 1287 dd27 · 1289 1aa2 · 1294 ed82 · 1298+1300 f124/S10 · 1306 1086 · 1307 e951 · 1308 f124 leak
fix · 1315 f124 hygiene · 1316 2ca9 · 1317 34cd
CLOSED (17): 043f 84aa b718 9ac2 12e4 e3cd f81d 635f 62ac 7fe2 1aa2 dd27 0d76 e951 1086 (+ f124 2ca9 34cd
closing).

## THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT THING FOR THE NEXT SESSION
**eb6es plan is CERTIFIED and the cutover is authorised** ("You are authorized to execute live cutovers
once the code is complete, fully tested, and the cutover is unblocked" — operator, this session). It took
THREE reviews. The second one found a SHOWSTOPPER that would have taken the production gate down:
  Dockerfile.reviewbot:83 installs `--extra agents --extra reviewbot` but NOT `--extra bedrock`, while
  pyproject.toml:133-135 defines bedrock as a DISTINCT extra. bedrock_model.py:61-63 raises a typed
  LLMConfigError on the missing import. With NO cross-provider fallback by design, the LLM-Review gate
  would have stopped voting on every landing the moment the cutover took effect.
  THE FAILURE SHAPE IS PARTIALLY MASKED: pyproject.toml:93 puts boto3 in the image, so the boto3-based
  region pre-check at bedrock_model.py:76-79 SUCCEEDS and only the provider import fails. A "can this
  container reach Bedrock with boto3?" probe reports healthy. PROBE THE IMPORT, not reachability.
  WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: 1aa2 proved all three gates clean on Bedrock — LOCALLY, where [dev] installs every
  extra. A local proof cannot see a container packaging gap. Same blind-spot pattern as a574s
  --region-everywhere runbook.
The third review blocked on the terraform alarms metric source. RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT: AWS/Bedrock
already publishes InvocationClientErrors and Invocations in account 896586841071, dimensioned by ModelId
(values include us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 from our own traffic). So the alarm is metric-math over
NATIVE metrics, observability.sh STAYS out of scope, and the dimensionless-on-both-sides contract from
monitoring_s4b/s5 does NOT apply — a native metric is AWS-dimensioned and the alarm must MATCH it. I also
added a criterion that the alarm be proven NOT in INSUFFICIENT_DATA: an alarm on a metric nothing publishes
is indistinguishable from a healthy one by state name.
uv.lock ALREADY carries the bedrock extra and `uv lock --check` passes — no regeneration needed. uv.lock
declares bedrock mutually exclusive with eval, which is fine because the image installs neither eval nor dev.

## OPERATOR DECISIONS ADDED THIS SESSION — do not relitigate
* CUTOVERS AUTHORISED once code is complete, fully tested, and unblocked.
* DO NOT HOLD LANDINGS for autodeploy churn: "If the churn naturally resolves itself, it is worth it to
  continue making progress on this epic as rapidly as possible."
* THREE permanent production switches, not one: the repo config / local environment (1aa2, DONE), the AWS
  review bot (eb6e), and the external integration tests in CI (f124/S10, DONE).
* External integration should test MULTIPLE providers for live-grounded confidence, NOT flip to Bedrock —
  a matrix, not a switch. And CI is a good place to exercise REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE, so the override path
  gets live coverage instead of being hand-exercised.
* The IAM role rebar-external-ci-bedrock must be scoped to MAIN ONLY: "External integration tests are not
  run on branches and our repo closes PRs with a redirect to Gerrit." sub is now an EXACT StringEquals on
  repo:navapbc/rebar:ref:refs/heads/main — no glob at all.
* The usage-log pricing defect is a REGRESSION from this epic and belongs INSIDE it: Anthropic prices
  displayed correctly before the provider-qualification work.
* A new funded OPENAI_API_KEY was set as a repository secret.

## WHAT I CREATED IN AWS (operator-approved)
IAM role `rebar-external-ci-bedrock` + inline policy `rebar-external-ci-bedrock-converse`
(bedrock:InvokeModel + InvokeModelWithResponseStream on anthropic.claude-* foundation models and
*.anthropic.claude-* inference profiles), no managed policies. Trust: aud=sts.amazonaws.com,
repository=navapbc/rebar, sub EXACTLY repo:navapbc/rebar:ref:refs/heads/main. Repo VARIABLES (not secrets):
AWS_BEDROCK_CI_ROLE_ARN, AWS_BEDROCK_CI_REGION=us-east-1. Definition of record:
infra/runbooks/bedrock-ci-oidc.md. NOTE the role was created by CLI so terraform has NO state for it —
committed HCL would plan a CREATE and collide; adoption needs `terraform import` in the same change.

## S10 IS FULLY VERIFIED — all three arms green, with the anti-vacuous-green oracle
Run 30846201728, head d4095763e (verified to contain the fix BEFORE reading any result):
  anthropic executed=14 skipped=1 · bedrock executed=15 skipped=0 · openai executed=14 skipped=1
The leak it found: overlays set only [llm.model_classes], but cfg.model is a SECOND resolution path —
config.py:575 falls back to DEFAULT_MODEL, the bare literal "claude-opus-4-8", which infers anthropic. Three
tests read cfg.model and so called direct Anthropic on EVERY arm. Fixed by adding `[llm] model` to each
overlay + switching review_skeleton.yamls ladder to class names.
TWO TESTS WERE COMPLICIT, and this is the transferable lesson:
  `test_each_overlay_sets_only_the_model_classes_table` asserted set(data["llm"]) == {"model_classes"} — so
  the fix COULD NOT LAND without that test failing. A test was ENFORCING the bug.
  `test_every_model_class_resolves_to_the_declared_provider` PASSED on all three arms while those arms
  called Anthropic, because it only checked the three CLASS names and never cfg.model. Its docstring claims
  to catch exactly this. An assertion over the wrong surface certifies the gap.

## MY OWN MISTAKES THIS SESSION — all corrected, all worth not repeating
1. I DISPATCHED A CI RUN 15 SECONDS AFTER A GERRIT SUBMIT. The GitHub mirror had not replicated, so the run
   tested PRE-FIX code (head f2b2d0b41) and failed identically to before — I nearly read that as my fix not
   working. ALWAYS assert the runs head SHA contains your change before reading any result.
2. I BROKE main. My leak-fix embedded the raw CI run id in seven comments;
   test_comment_hygiene_guard::test_the_real_tree_is_clean is in the default selection, so EVERY CI run on
   main failed until it was fixed. Another session fixed the .py half (36e986c188); 1315 was my rebased
   remainder. THE GATE ONLY SCANS PYTHON — a rot-prone ref in .toml or workflow .yaml is invisible to it,
   which is why four survived a green gate.
3. `commit --amend -F <file>` DROPS THE Change-Id, the hook stamps a fresh one, and Gerrit opens a NEW
   change. Orphaned 1299 and 1312 that way; both abandoned with reasons. Carry the Change-Id in the file.
4. I corrupted a TOML by `replace(anchor, ..., 1)` where the first textual match was inside a COMMENT.
   Anchor on the real header line.
5. I patched capabilities.py in the SHARED store worktree while another jobs gate was reading it. Audited
   the verdict afterwards (it cited nothing from the patched file) but that was luck. One worktree per job.
6. My chained script and the operator both dispatched the same workflow 2 seconds apart — double live spend
   across three providers. Cancelled mine. The workflow declares NO concurrency group.
7. I hit the zsh `set -- $var` no-word-splitting trap the previous handoff explicitly warned about.

## CORRECTIONS SUBAGENTS MADE TO ME — three, each worth more than the code
* 2ca9: my plan said a blind split(":") would break Bedrock because the remainder is not genai-prices AWS
  id shape. FALSE — it prices fine at $0.00495. The real case is the VERSIONED id
  anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0, which a split reduces to "0". Conclusion survived, reason did not.
* 34cd: the bot ALREADY drains its queue (app.py:117 + stop_grace_period 1320s), so webhook reviews are
  protected. reconcile.py:223 awaits review_and_vote INLINE, outside it, and THE RECONCILER IS THE RETRY
  PATH — so the self-heal mechanism is the unprotected one. I had told the operator this "self-heals
  benignly"; the retry is what dies.
* eb6e rewrite: I claimed the S4b alarm had no thresholds. It does (monitoring_s4b.tf period=300,
  evaluation_periods=1, threshold=0). And finding 4 was half-stale — the per-pass split HAS landed, which
  INVERTS the hazard from "one knob for four passes" to "a scalar would COLLAPSE a split that now exists".

## LOG EXTRACTION THAT ACTUALLY WORKS (three of my attempts failed)
GitHub serves NO logs until a run fully COMPLETES — not via `gh run view --log`, not via the API. Once
complete: `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/<RUN>/logs > logs.zip`, then unzip with a Python zipfile
loop (macOS unzip chokes on the em-dash in a step filename and reports a bogus "disk full").

## ADR MATERIAL FOR 8625 IS PRESERVED ON THE TICKET
Four comments, ~96KB, verified byte-identical: 47 decisions + 5 standing operator decisions; rejected
alternatives WITH their evidence; operational findings; every specific way docs/llm-framework.md is now
wrong; the tier model; and an honesty ledger. READ THE LEDGER FIRST — it records that TWO OF 8625S OWN
PREMISES ARE FALSE (its line refs are stale; its ":131-133 only true in S4" claim is stale the other way
since S4 landed), and that the epics "first_class = full fidelity" retry/timeout parity claim is UNBACKED
BY CODE (bedrock_model.py:88 is just BedrockProvider(region_name=region); no botocore Config, no
aws_read_timeout anywhere).
